Article Title: ‘Detain, arrest, we won't be intimidated’: CJP's team held again, vows to continue Delhi protest
Article Text:
CJP leaders detained on Sunday amid call to continue protest

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Sunday alleged that Delhi Police detained its leaders during protests demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The party vowed not to be intimidated by the action.In a series of posts on X, CJP named Ankit Bharadwaj, Anam, Mukesh All-rounder, Balakrishna and Sudhir Sangwan as those detained while allegedly protesting peacefully. The organisation also claimed that its team was being harassed by the police.“Detain us, arrest us, do whatever you can! We will not be intimidated. This is just the beginning. We will continue fighting until all our demands are met,” CJP post reads.In another post, the organisation alleged that the police action against its members was continuing. “Brutality Continues! Delhi Police have detained CJP’s team and are harassing us,” it said.The party also declared that it would not back down, describing the developments as “the beginning of the end of this dictatorship”.On Saturday, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were reportedly detained at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport after arriving from Mumbai.They were released earlier on Sunday, on condition that they would not "breach peace" for a year, CJP legal affairs head Ratna Singh said.More than 7,000 protesters were also detained at multiple locations, preventing them from reaching Jantar Mantar, police sources said. Several opposition leaders, including former chief ministers Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee, Pinarayi Vijayan and Manik Sarkar, were also detained while attempting to join the protest.The CJP renewed its call for a protest at Jantar Mantar on Sunday as police continued security arrangements across the city. More than 30,000 police and paramilitary personnel were to be deployed, according to the report.
Article Summary: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Sunday alleged that Delhi Police detained its leaders during protests. The party vowed not to be intimidated by the action. CJP renewed its call for a protest at Jantar Mantar on Sunday as police continued security arrangements.

Article Title: The period cycle: What happens in your body beyond the five days of bleeding
Article Text:
The days leading up to a period can be just as challenging as the bleeding itself.

What your body goes through during the entire cycle.

Beyond the five days

“Chill! It’s just periods. You’ll feel better in a couple of days.”But do women really get better in three to five days or are they caught in a recurring loop of exhaustion, mood swings and hormonal shifts that returns month after month from their first period till end.From hormonal fluctuations and ovulation to fatigue, bloating and premenstrual symptoms, the menstrual cycle is a month-long process that extends far beyond the days of bleeding. Yet, what happens inside the body between periods remains poorly understood by many women.For some, menstruation brings severe cramps, exhaustion and an overwhelming need to be left alone. Others struggle with bloating, back pain, irritability or difficulty concentrating at work. And for many, the days leading up to a period can be just as challenging as the bleeding itself.“I feel like somebody is constantly stabbing me with a sword, not even a knife, in my stomach,” says Sasha Singh, describing her experience of menstruation.“Emotionally, I am so annoyed that eye rolls become the only friend that day. The Luteal phase is the worst for me, an indication of days ahead,” she added.For Shivanghi, the physical discomfort comes with an emotional toll.“I feel like I need to punch whoever is talking to me and cry all the time. Physically its like my insides are getting drained and sawed repeatedly. I feel the first day and the day before that are the most painful.”Their experiences highlight how differently women can experience the menstrual cycle, both physically and emotionally. They also raise a larger question: What happens inside the body when there is no bleeding?Menstruation is the shedding of the uterine lining through the vagina when pregnancy has not occurred. The bleeding contains blood and tissue from the lining of the uterus, also called the endometrium.Periods generally last between three and seven days, although the duration and amount of bleeding vary. Menstruation usually begins during puberty, most commonly between the ages of 11 and 14, though it can start earlier or later. It continues through the reproductive years until menopause, which typically occurs between the ages of 45 and 55.The menstrual cycle, however, covers the entire interval from the first day of one period to the first day of the next.A cycle is often described as lasting 28 days, but this is only an average. Many adults have cycles that fall within a range of approximately 21 to 35 days, and cycle length can vary with age and individual circumstances.The cycle is regulated by hormones that coordinate activity between the brain, the ovaries and the uterus. Its four commonly described phases are menstruation, the follicular phase, ovulation and the luteal phase.Importantly, these phases are not four completely separate stages. The follicular phase begins on the first day of menstruation and continues until ovulation, meaning the first two phases overlap.The menstrual cycle begins on the first day of menstrual bleeding. When pregnancy has not occurred, the levels of hormones that support the uterine lining fall, prompting the lining to shed.The uterus contracts to help expel this tissue, which can cause cramps in the lower abdomen and sometimes pain in the lower back. Some women also experience bloating, headaches, fatigue, breast discomfort or changes in mood.According to Priyanka, the first two days can be particularly difficult. “During my period, I usually feel physically tired, bloated and uncomfortable, with severe cramps and lower back pain. Emotionally, I tend to feel more irritable, sensitive and overwhelmed than usual. The most challenging phase for me is the few days leading up to my period the Luteal phase, when PMS symptoms like mood swings, fatigue and bloating are at their peak. The first two days of my period can also be difficult,” she added.Hormone levels, particularly those of oestrogen and progesterone, are relatively low at the beginning of the cycle. But this does not mean that the body's reproductive processes have stopped. As menstruation begins, hormones are already signalling the ovaries to start developing follicles for the next stage.For most women, some discomfort during menstruation can be managed with appropriate measures. However, severe pain that interferes with daily activities should not automatically be dismissed as a normal part of having periods.This phase starts on the first day of menstruation and continues until ovulation.During this time, the pituitary gland releases follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), which stimulates the development of follicles in the ovaries. Each follicle contains an immature egg, and usually one becomes dominant and continues to mature.As the follicle develops, it produces increasing amounts of oestrogen. This hormone helps rebuild and thicken the uterine lining after menstruation.The changes are taking place even after the bleeding stops, although they may not produce obvious symptoms.Some women report feeling more energetic or focused during the days after their period. Others do not notice any clear difference. These experiences can vary from one person to another and even from one cycle to the next.Vijaya notices significant changes in her energy and concentration around her cycle. “Oh yes!! It changes drastically. Energy drops, concentration is hindered. Sleep becomes overpowering, as if body is on energy saver mode.”However, it is important not to assume that every change in energy or mood is caused by menstrual hormones. Sleep, stress, nutrition, underlying health conditions and other factors can also influence how someone feels.The follicular phase illustrates why the menstrual cycle is more than a monthly episode of bleeding. While the body prepares an egg for possible release, the uterine lining is also being rebuilt.As the dominant follicle matures, rising oestrogen levels help trigger a surge in luteinising hormone (LH). This surge causes ovulation, when the ovary releases a mature egg.Ovulation is often described as occurring around day 14 of a 28-day cycle, but its timing varies. It does not necessarily happen on the same day for everyone, or even in every cycle for the same person.After its release, the egg enters the fallopian tube, where it may be fertilised by sperm. The egg usually remains capable of fertilisation for approximately 12 to 24 hours. However, pregnancy can occur from sex in the days leading up to ovulation because sperm can survive in the reproductive tract for several days.Some women notice changes around ovulation, while some experience mild pain on one side of the lower abdomen. Others may notice no obvious physical changes.There is also considerable variation in whether women report changes in mood, energy or sexual desire around this time. These experiences should not be treated as universal signs of ovulation.Understanding ovulation is important not only for those trying to conceive but also for anyone seeking to understand the timing of their cycle. Calendar estimates and period-tracking apps can help identify patterns, but they cannot always predict the exact day of ovulation.After ovulation, the follicle that released the egg transforms into a structure called the corpus luteum. It produces progesterone, along with some oestrogen, to help maintain the uterine lining in preparation for a possible pregnancy.If pregnancy does not occur, the corpus luteum breaks down. Progesterone and oestrogen levels fall, triggering changes that eventually lead to the shedding of the uterine lining and the start of the next period.For some women, the luteal phase brings premenstrual syndrome (PMS), with symptoms such as bloating, breast tenderness, headaches, fatigue, irritability, food cravings and disturbed sleep.The intensity varies, with some experiencing mild discomfort while others struggle with symptoms that affect their work and daily lives. In severe cases, symptoms may indicate premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD), which can cause significant emotional and physical distress.The emotional effects can be difficult to explain. “Getting irritated all the time and crying for no reason. It feels like everyone is being rude and they all hate me,” says Shivanghi.Priyanka also reports increased irritability and anxiety, while Vijaya notices a drop in energy and concentration. Hormonal fluctuations may also coincide with acne, changes in appetite and digestive issues such as bloating, constipation or diarrhoea.Persistent acne, unexplained hair loss, increased facial hair, substantial weight changes or ongoing digestive problems can also be automatically attributed to the menstrual cycle. However, severe or persistent symptoms that interfere with daily life warrant medical assessment.The effects of the menstrual cycle can extend beyond reproductive organs. Changes in oestrogen and progesterone may influence several bodily functions, although the extent of these effects differs between individuals.According to Dr Asha Susawat, senior obstetrician and gynaecologist at Cocoon Hospital, Jaipur, hormonal fluctuations can influence how women feel throughout the cycle.“While the hormonal fluctuations will be much more impactful than just your bleeding pattern, their importance will vary from woman to woman. For some, high levels of oestrogen before ovulation make them feel more energetic. Others will not perceive any significant differences. Following the occurrence of ovulation, the progesterone hormone increases the temperature levels in the body and may affect the sleep pattern. As the woman starts to bleed, some may feel sleepy, irritable, nervous, food craving, among other symptoms such as breakout, bloating, constipation, or diarrhoea. Nevertheless, not all the factors are felt by everyone and need more diagnoses.”Dr Rhythm Bhalla, senior consultant in obstetrics and gynaecology at Cocoon Hospital, Chandigarh, similarly notes that symptoms can begin before the next period arrives.“The physical effects of menstrual cycle on women may start long before the upcoming period. Variations in levels of oestrogen and progesterone affect moods, sleep, eating and energy levels. However, there is no standard experience in this regard since some women feel better before ovulation whereas some start experiencing fatigue, poor sleep, cravings and irritability prior to the onset of the period. Women may start experiencing acne and bloating, while digestive problems may turn into constipation or diarrhoea before the period starts. There may be minor symptoms but serious problems should not be overlooked.”Despite menstruation being a regular part of life for millions of women, understanding of the complete menstrual cycle remains uneven.Many learn the basics at school or at home but receive little information about ovulation, hormonal fluctuations and the physical and emotional changes that can occur throughout the menstrual cycle.When asked whether they knew that hormonal changes continue throughout the month, even when they are not bleeding, the responses revealed varying levels of awareness.Vijaya said, “Yes. The whole cycle is in process and goes beyond just shedding blood. There is constant hormonal fluctuations which ultimately affects the energy and motivation throughout the lifetime.”Prisha Patnaik responded, “Yes, I think 4 phases?” while Shivanghi said, “I have a broad idea, like the luteal, follicular phases and all. Not really informed about the details.”Their responses point to a distinction between knowing that the menstrual cycle involves hormonal changes and understanding how these changes unfold across its different phases.For many, school provides only the basics, leaving them to turn to family members, friends or online resources for more information. Others have to seek answers on their own.Vijaya said, “I didn't learn about periods at home, it was only until I got them did I have the conversation. In school it was only what textbook had to offer, they didn't even teach about pads etc.”Priyanka said, “I learnt the basics at school, but very little about hormonal changes and their impact on our bodies. One common misconception I've encountered is that periods are just about bleeding, when they actually affect our physical and emotional well-being throughout the month.”Sneha said, “I don’t have much to say about how periods were discussed at school. I got most of my information at home and from Google, which I explored out of curiosity.”These experiences underline the need for menstrual-health education that goes beyond explaining bleeding.Girls and boys need age-appropriate information about the menstrual cycle, reproductive health, common symptoms and when medical attention may be necessary.The gap is not just in what women are taught, but also in how menstruation is discussed. For Sasha, her first lessons about periods at school offered little insight into the subject.Years later, she encountered another misconception in the workplace, where her mood was sometimes attributed to menstruation.“When I worked in an all-boys work desk, I was often asked if I was on periods if I was not in a cheerful mood. Bad mood can be a product of multiple things, not just periods,” she added.In many parts of India, menstruation remains a subject surrounded by stigma and silence. Some women continue to face restrictions on entering kitchens, touching utensils, participating in religious activities or discussing periods openly.Pari (name changed), from Assam, describes the restrictions followed in her household."On the three days of my period, I sit and sleep on the floor. I eat on a separate plate as I am not allowed to enter the kitchen or touch any utensil or other furniture. I do not touch any male member be it my father, brother or husband. These customs have been followed for a very long time in my household and me, my mother and sister have applied the same in our lives."Her account reflects how cultural practices can shape women's experiences of menstruation beyond the physical symptoms themselves.Yash Sonkar points to the gaps in menstrual-health education, saying, “Menstruation isn’t even properly explained in our school curriculum… teachers skip the chapters at times.”For Trisha, the problem goes beyond inadequate education to the stigma surrounding menstruation. One of the most persistent misconceptions she has encountered, she says, is that periods make women “impure”.Vijaya's experience reflects how deeply such beliefs can become embedded in everyday life. “As for misconceptions, it's hard to think of one that I might not have been forced on. Days on which I can cut my nails, touching the pickle, touching gods or even mentioning it in front of a male entity,” she says, recalling the restrictions associated with menstruation.These beliefs can persist through seemingly ordinary practices, from discouraging women from entering places of worship to treating menstruation as something that must be kept out of sight.Even the habit of wrapping sanitary napkins discreetly or avoiding conversations about periods can reinforce the idea that menstruation is something to hide rather than a normal biological process.The menstrual cycle is regulated by a complex interaction between the brain, the ovaries and the uterus. Several factors can interfere with this process, affecting ovulation, the timing of periods and the amount of bleeding.Dr Susawat explains that stress can affect the hormones involved in ovulation, potentially delaying periods or causing them to be missed. Thyroid disorders can influence cycle length and bleeding patterns, while PCOS may interfere with regular ovulation and lead to irregular or absent periods.Age is another factor. Cycles may be irregular during the years after menstruation first begins and may change again during perimenopause, the transition towards menopause. Hormonal contraception can also alter bleeding patterns, depending on the method used.Dr Bhalla said that the cycle depends on several systems working together. “Periods are the result of interaction between the brain, the ovaries and the uterus; there are many things that might interfere in this interaction. Stress, combined with big changes in weight or poor eating habits, may lead to ovulation delay,” Bhalla said.“Thyroid issues may cause changes in bleeding amount and frequency. In PCOS, ovulation may be less frequent and make periods irregular. The menstrual problems can occur during the period of adolescence before the beginning of menopause. As hormonal contraceptives have an impact on the level of reproductive hormones and uterine lining in some form, so the bleeding can be less, spotting or absence of periods can occur,” she added.This means that a change in the menstrual cycle does not necessarily indicate a serious health problem, but persistent changes should not be ignored.A healthcare professional may consider factors such as stress, medication, pregnancy, thyroid function and PCOS when assessing irregular periods.Although changes in mood, energy and physical comfort may occur throughout the menstrual cycle, not every symptom should be attributed to hormones.According to Dr Susawat, excessive bleeding between periods, bleeding after sexual intercourse, persistent pelvic pain or pain during intercourse should be evaluated. Unusual vaginal discharge accompanied by an odour, irritation or fever also warrants medical attention.She highlights that women should seek an assessment if their menstrual pattern changes significantly or if they miss periods for three months. If pregnancy is possible, a missed period may be a reason to take a pregnancy test.Dr Bhalla similarly advises that frequent bleeding between cycles, bleeding after intercourse, persistent pelvic pain and unusual discharge accompanied by itching, a bad odour or fever should not be ignored.“This can be explained through the normal process of a woman. Abnormal bleeding that occurs frequently in between cycles, or bleeding following sexual intercourse, or constant pain in the pelvis area or during sexual intercourse should be dealt with appropriately. Unusual vaginal discharge accompanied by signs such as itching, bad odor and fever should be attended to. Irregular periods which result in absence of menstruation for over three months should also be considered and an examination carried out. This should be done as early as possible if pregnancy is one of the probable causes. Severe pelvic pain in addition to bleeding, missing periods and fainting should be handled as a matter of urgency. Excessive vaginal bleeding accompanied by weakness, dizziness and difficulty breathing should also be handled urgently,” she said.Other warning signs include bleeding that lasts longer than seven days, very heavy bleeding, severe or worsening menstrual pain and symptoms that interfere with work, studies or daily activities.Heavy bleeding can lead to iron deficiency anaemia, particularly when it occurs repeatedly. Severe menstrual pain may also be associated with conditions such as endometriosis or adenomyosis, while irregular cycles may warrant assessment for PCOS, thyroid disorders or other underlying causes.Severe pelvic pain accompanied by a missed period, bleeding or faintness requires urgent medical assessment, particularly when pregnancy is possible.The key is to recognise the difference between a symptom that occurs occasionally and one that is persistent, severe or unusual for the individual.The World Health Organisation (WHO) recognises menstrual health as more than a matter of managing bleeding. It includes access to accurate information, affordable menstrual products, safe sanitation facilities, appropriate healthcare and the ability to participate in everyday life without stigma.The WHO has also highlighted the limited availability of high-quality scientific research on menstruation. Better research and education can help improve care, support health policies and challenge myths surrounding the menstrual cycle.The organisation estimates that around 500 million people who menstruate worldwide lack access to the full range of menstrual-health materials, facilities and services. It has also cited emerging national data indicating that around 39% of schools provide menstrual-health education.These gaps matter because a lack of information can prevent women from recognising symptoms that require medical attention. It can also make it harder for them to discuss menstrual difficulties without embarrassment or fear of being dismissed.The menstrual cycle is a continuous process shaped by hormones, reproductive health, age and individual circumstances.While some women experience significant physical and emotional changes throughout the month, others notice little variation beyond menstruation.Understanding these differences can help women recognise their own patterns, question symptoms that disrupt daily life and seek medical advice when necessary.Better menstrual-health education can also challenge misconceptions and make conversations about periods less uncomfortable.Men, too, have a role to play. When partners understand the physical and emotional changes women may experience throughout the cycle, they can offer greater empathy, support and understanding instead of dismissing symptoms or attributing every change in mood to menstruation.
Article Summary: The days leading up to a period can be just as challenging as the bleeding itself. Menstruation is the shedding of the uterine lining through the vagina when pregnancy has not occurred. The bleeding contains blood and tissue from the lining of the uterus, also called the endometrium.

Article Title: Suvendu eyes Bengal sweep: Can Mamata, Congress unite to challenge BJP?
Article Text:
West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari

Bypolls have usually favoured the ruling party

Suvendu's promise

Why BJP's victories still matter

Allegations of electoral excesses

BJP supporters in Rejinagar

What's next for the Opposition?

Mamata Banerjee's political journey before becoming CM

Municipal elections: The next big battle

Road to 2029

Former Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee detained during protest in New Delhi

"We are set to win 42 out of 42 in the 2029 Lok Sabha election." West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari had made this grandiose claim even before the Nandigram and Rejinagar bypoll results. A visibly buoyant Adhikari reiterated the target after his party swept both seats. Victories in both constituencies were expected, yet the margins, particularly in Rejinagar, where roughly 70% of voters are Muslim, came as a revelation. With the all-important Kolkata and Howrah municipal polls likely to be held in late November, there is a perception that the BJP may win handsomely. It is up to the Opposition to put up a spirited fight.What may give the Opposition some solace is the fact that bypolls, at least over the last decade or so, have followed an extremely predictable pattern in Bengal. Between the 2021 and 2026 Assembly elections, Trinamool won 20 of the 21 Assembly bypolls held in the state. Its dominance was particularly striking in 2024, when it swept all 12 by-elections, including four seats previously held by BJP legislators.In July 2024, Trinamool wrested Raiganj, Ranaghat Dakshin and Bagdah from the BJP despite the latter's electoral strength in these areas during the Lok Sabha election just weeks earlier.In November, TMC captured Madarihat, which the BJP had held since 2016. Even in June 2025, less than a year before its Assembly rout, Trinamool retained Kaliganj by more than 50,000 votes.There have been exceptions to the incumbent's advantage. In 2023, Congress , supported by the Left, defeated the ruling TMC in Sagardighi by nearly 23,000 votes. However, the MLA concerned, Bayron Biswas, soon joined TMC.In Nandigram, BJP's Hasi Rani Rath defeated Congress candidate Milan Pradhan, who had Mamata's support, by 1,22,753 votes. In Rejinagar, BJP's Shankharavh Sarkar defeated Aam Janata Unnayan Party candidate Golam Nabi Azad, son of party founder Humayun Kabir, by more than 75,000 votes.In both constituencies, BJP polled more votes than all its opponents combined. Rejinagar witnessed notable outreach from the CM, with Suvendu even saying that Muslims did not need to chant "Jai Shri Ram". He also urged them to turn over a new leaf and extend a hand of friendship to the new government.Following the result, Adhikari attributed BJP's success partly to support from beneficiaries of the Annapurna welfare scheme, under which eligible women receive ₹3,000 per month. Whether the BJP can really secure a share of the Muslim vote in elections with bigger stakes remains to be seen. But if it does, Suvendu's dream of a clean sweep in the Lok Sabha election may well look more realistic.The Opposition, though, has refused to grant legitimacy to the Assembly bypolls, citing alleged malpractices by the ruling machinery. Bengal Congress president Subhankar Sarkar demanded fresh elections in both constituencies, alleging booth capturing, intimidation, bogus voting and the forcible removal of polling agents. AJUP, which had won the seat previously, alleged that its candidate received zero votes in 33 booths and just one vote in another 19 booths. Mamata's TMC faction made similar allegations of rigging, while the rival Trinamool faction and the Left also complained about polling agents being prevented from functioning.In Nandigram, Congress candidate Milan Pradhan alleged that party agents had been driven out of booths and voters prevented from voting. His earlier arrest in connection with an old case related to the Nandigram land movement had already prompted allegations of political harassment.BJP rejected the rigging allegations, maintaining that polling was peaceful. The Election Commission described voting as largely peaceful despite receiving complaints. One widely circulated claim that BJP had received more votes than the number of registered voters at a Rejinagar booth was subsequently rebutted by election officials, who said the original electorate figure was incorrect.Such allegations are not new to Bengal's electoral politics, one of the reasons why the opposition have frequently asked for central forces to conduct polls. The 2018 panchayat elections witnessed widespread reports of violence and intimidation. More than a third of the seats were won uncontested, overwhelmingly by Trinamool, amid allegations that opposition candidates had been prevented from filing nominations. A year later, the BJP increased its Lok Sabha tally in Bengal from two seats in 2014 to 18 in 2019.Political observers have linked that breakthrough partly to resentment over the conduct of the panchayat polls. Very recently, Abhishek Banerjee’s Diamond Harbour model of winning by record margin of votes had also come under scrutiny. For BJP though, barely a few months into power, the chances of pushback to any alleged excesses remain relatively modest.The INDIA bloc has upped the ante in the capital, demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged vote manipulation during the SIR process. Leaders such as Rahul Gandhi, Mamata Banerjee and even those from the Left have been sharing the stage. With a common goal, the confluence is organic. But the state-level dynamics are very different, something that has affected the INDIA alliance for a long time.An INDIA alliance is unlikely to become a reality in Bengal, with Left and TMC cadres rarely seeing eye to eye. An alliance between Mamata's TMC and Congress remains an open question, with state leaders of the grand old party lukewarm about giving space to a leader who did not allow them much room to grow while in power.Mamata came to power in 2011 in alliance with Congress, but the two soon parted ways. Since then, the parties have hardly worked together politically, until this by-election. There have been several overtures from Congress in the past, but these were rebuffed by the then West Bengal CM, who wanted to maximise her political capital. Now that the script has flipped, Congress may not give in so easily.Former state Congress president Pradip Bhattacharya disclosed in September that the state leadership had advised against a proposed bypoll arrangement under which Congress would contest Nandigram and Mamata's Trinamool would fight Rejinagar. Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury's recent invitation to Mamata to return to Congress with her remaining MLAs and MPs came with a condition about leaving behind her political baggage, widely interpreted as a reference to Abhishek Banerjee.Even the Nandigram understanding was not a formal seat-sharing arrangement. Mamata supported Milan Pradhan after her faction's candidate withdrew. In Rejinagar, both parties contested separately. Many Congress leaders believe that it is time to rebuild the party in the state when opposition space is up for grabs. The BJP is still getting to grips with governance, and teething troubles in several areas, including the rollout of government schemes, have made headlines.The organisational crisis within Trinamool adds another dimension. Following the Assembly defeat, the party split into rival factions, prompting the Election Commission to temporarily freeze its original name and symbol. The Mamata-led faction and the Ritabrata Banerjee-led Democratic Trinamool Congress contested under different identities in the bypolls. Neither performed well. In Rejinagar, Mamata's faction received 3,847 votes, while Democratic Trinamool polled 2,044.The Left, meanwhile, continues to face the challenge of translating political visibility into electoral support. Younger leaders such as Satarup Ghosh, Dipshita Dhar and Srijan Bhattacharya have attracted attention, particularly on social media, but the party's electoral recovery remains limited.There were, however, modest improvements in the latest bypolls. In Nandigram, the CPI's Santi Gopal Giri increased his tally from 2,997 votes in May to 5,779. Congress also improved its vote count in both constituencies, although the Nandigram comparison is complicated by Mamata's support for its candidate.The immediate electoral focus now shifts to the Kolkata and Howrah municipal polls, where voting is tentatively expected in late November. The stakes extend far beyond the two Assembly bypolls.In the 2021 Kolkata Municipal Corporation election, Trinamool won 134 of 144 wards, securing more than 72% of the votes. BJP won just three wards and Congress two. Interestingly, the Left Front, with nearly 12% of the vote, finished ahead of BJP in vote share despite winning fewer seatstThe forthcoming election will also be fought on a substantially altered map. Kolkata's wards have increased from 144 to 209, and Howrah's from 50 to 68. For both factions of TMC, this election will be the first major test of who enjoys greater public support. For Mamata Banerjee, south Kolkata remains her pocket borough, and following the humiliating defeat in Bhabanipur, she would be desperate to turn around her fortunes. For Firhad Hakim and others, it will be an opportunity to prove that they can win on their own without Didi's support.Congress and the Left have long been marginal forces in both Kolkata and Howrah, barring a few pockets. The Left appears inclined to contest independently in several areas, although the CPM has encouraged local discussions with Congress. Some Congress district leaders, meanwhile, have argued that the party should contest all 209 Kolkata wards on its own.The decisions are yet to be finalised, leaving Congress with a difficult choice between rebuilding independently, cooperating with the Left and exploring an understanding with Mamata.Nationally, Rahul Gandhi's success in rallying different INDIA bloc parties in the campaign demanding the resignation of the CEC has done his popularity no harm. The bonhomie between Sonia Gandhi and Mamata Banerjee at the recent press conference was there for everyone to see. They have maintained cordial personal relations despite the ebbs and flows in their political exchanges. But the political calculations in Bengal remain very different. Rahul's pointed attacks on Trinamool over corruption during the Assembly campaign had reinforced the Congress's adversarial position in the state. For local Congress workers, a sudden statewide alliance with Mamata would require a significant political adjustment. Didi however, remains in the frontlines in the protest against Election Commission and was detained on Saturday even as Rahul Gandhi skipped the protest and went to Chennai.At the same time, Mamata faces one of the most difficult phases of her political career, while the BJP confronts increasingly coordinated opposition protests at the national level. Hence the political equations could well change. After the municipal elections in Kolkata and Howrah, polls in more than 100 other civic bodies are expected next year, followed by panchayat polls in 2028 and the Lok Sabha election in 2029. Those who have power in the grassroots are likely to have a headstart in the Lok Sabha election.Suvendu has already set his sights on winning all 42 Lok Sabha seats in Bengal. Such a result would have significant implications for the BJP's national parliamentary tally. For Congress, the calculation is therefore not confined to the revival of its Bengal organisation. Its leadership must also consider the wider political ramifications of allowing the BJP a free-run in the state.For the Opposition, national unity over electoral issues is one thing. Building an effective political arrangement in Bengal is quite another. The coming municipal elections will provide the first major opportunity to see whether those differences can be bridged.
Article Summary: West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari had made grandiose claim even before the Nandigram and Rejinagar bypoll results. Bypolls, at least over the last decade or so, have followed an extremely predictable pattern in Bengal. Trinamool won 20 of the 21 Assembly bypolls.

NEW DELHI: Soon after touching down at Delhi Airport around 10.30 am Saturday with Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) representatives Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka on board, the pilots operating AI 2428 were asked to head to a remote bay instead of a parking stand that is connected to an aerobridge. Article Title: Understand, don't just hear out a child in conflict with law: CJI
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant Saturday said a child in conflict with law must not only be heard but also be understood, since few young people can speak up for themselves before the police or any authority.Speaking on 10 years of the framing of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, Kant said very often, the child in conflict with law today was, only a little earlier, a child in need of care and protection whom we did not reach in time and that should be kept in mind while dealing with them."Our answer to such a predicament is restoration, not retribution. The Act presumes everyone below 18 to be innocent of any criminal intent, treats institutional care as a last resort, encourages diversion from formal proceedings, and prefers counselling, community service, and probation to confinement, while promising a fresh start. These choices flow from the Constitutional philosophy discernible from Articles 15(3) and 39 and also from the Convention on the Rights of the Child, which looks to the young assuming a constructive role in society. The 2015 Act thus makes a wager that a child given a second chance is far more likely to become a productive member of society than one branded as a criminal," he said.Supreme Court judge, Justice B V Nagarathna, who is heading SC's Juvenile Justice Committee, said adults have a duty to understand the anxieties of children. "We cannot be dismissive of their concerns, lest they feel alienated and rejected. The true measure of a society and its elders lies in how they deal with their children. We must ensure that we do not fail on that count. All children are ours and their distress is our distress too," Nagarathna said.
Article Summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said a child in conflict with law must not only be heard but also be understood. Few young people can speak up for themselves before the police or any authority. The Act presumes everyone below 18 to be innocent of any criminal intent, treats institutional care as a last resort.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: SIR strikes at heart of Constitution: Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan
Article Text:
File photo: Supreme Court of India Judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan (PTI Photo)

Detaching right to vote from citizen is like taking soul out of body: Bhuyan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Launching a scathing attack on special intensive revision (SIR) that has resulted in large-scale deletion of names from voter lists across states, Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Sunday said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution.Discounting the reasons given by govt and EC to justify SIR, which was upheld in the case of the revision of rolls in West Bengal by SC with modifications, Justice Bhuyan said, "No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of Constitution. I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution."He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad.Nalsar students, who had opposed CJI Surya Kant's participation in the convocation ceremony recently, came in for praise from Justice Bhuyan.Also read| Democracy in peril as voters illegally ousted: Former SC judge Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman "One last word about the brilliant students of Nalsar. You have shown to the country and to the world what a university student, that too a student of law, should be. You are brilliant, you are bold, and you are brave," he said.Justice Bhuyan said a citizen’s right to vote was central to the holding of free and fair elections.“Except in the case of a dead voter, the name of a voter once enlisted in the electoral roll cannot be deleted without notice and hearing,” he added.The SC judge said the right to vote or be included in the voters’ list could not be detached from the persona of an Indian citizen.Also read: EC orders special drive to add genuine electors 'left out' during SIR “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added. Justice Bhuyan said the Indian Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens: citizens with voting rights and citizens without voting rights. “Any process which leads to wholesale disenfranchisement of Indian citizens, making them citizens without voting rights, would be violative of Articles 326 and 14 of Constitution of India,” he said.“If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens, making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary,” he added, his remarks coinciding with attacks on EC and govt over SIR by the opposition and others.Justice Bhuyan said the right to vote was intertwined with India’s years of struggle against foreign rule. “It is a manifestation of our freedom achieved after so much struggle and sacrifice. Article 326 (universal adult franchise) cannot be tinkered with at all. No authority can do it, no court can condone it. No one is above Constitution,” he said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution. He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad. “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added.

Lauren Kyle McDavid had always known she wanted to build something of her own, but turning her creative ideas into successful businesses came with a learning curve. The wife of Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid started with interior design before expanding into fashion, furniture, food and publishing. Behind that growth was a challenge she had to face early in her career: learning the business side of her creative work.That part of Lauren’s journey became more important as she took on more projects. By June 2025, she had several ventures under her name, while Connor had watched closely as she learned to turn her ideas into businesses. His support also came at a time when Lauren needed help taking her first company to the next level.Lauren Kyle spoke about her entrepreneurial journey in a June 8, 2025 interview with theScore. She explained that she had always pictured herself working for herself and had grown up around people who ran their own businesses. Her first major venture was Kyle & Co., an interior design company that gave her a place to turn her ideas into a career.However, creativity alone could not handle every part of running a growing company.Connor explained during the same theScore interview that creative people can sometimes struggle with the business side of their ideas. He had seen Lauren put considerable time and energy into Kyle & Co. and wanted to help her move the company forward.“I know how hard she works, and I know the time and energy that she puts into it,” Connor said while discussing Lauren’s business journey with theScore in June 2025.Connor McDavid had also given Lauren sessions with a business coach as a birthday gift a few years earlier. The support proved useful because Lauren wanted to grow beyond her first company without losing the creative side that had driven her from the beginning.Lauren later explained just how valuable that experience became for her. “Without my business coach, I definitely wouldn't be able to have this many businesses at one time,” she told theScore in June 2025. She said the coaching helped change her mindset and gave her a better understanding of how to grow as an entrepreneur.The business coaching became part of a much bigger change in Lauren’s career. By June 2025, her portfolio included Kyle & Co., Sports Club Atelier, Trove Living and Bar Trove, while she was also preparing a cookbook.Sports Club Atelier grew from Lauren’s interest in creating better-looking sports apparel. Trove Living gave her interior design work a furniture and showroom component, while Bar Trove brought her creative approach into the restaurant space in downtown Edmonton. Her cookbook followed the same idea by focusing on experiences such as dinner parties and girls’ weekends instead of simply dividing recipes into traditional categories.Lauren’s approach has remained consistent across those projects. She wants people to feel something when they enter a space, wear something she designed or experience something she created. That idea also explains why Connor has remained impressed by the work happening behind the scenes.“I get a front row seat to everything she’s building,” Connor said in theScore’s June 2025 profile.Lauren’s story is therefore about more than being Connor McDavid’s wife. Article Title: Sean Payton house: Inside $4.5M, 6,000 sq ft Belcaro mansion with oversized kitchen, primary suite fireplace and elevator where Denver Broncos coach lives with wife Skylene Montgomery

Sean Payton’s Saints era and Broncos comeback

Sean Payton was traded from the New Orleans Saints sidelines to the Denver Broncos franchise along with a 2024 third round draft pick.The Broncos head coach found himself a mansion in one of the Denver’s most-coveted residential neighborhoods. Belcaro is an established Denver neighborhood known for its upscale residences. He lives in the gated property with his wife, Skylene Montgomery.The 6,000 sq-ft property blends contemporary design with high-end residential features. The two-story home offers four bedrooms and six bathrooms. Its interiors are designed around spacious living rooms, custom finishes, and entertaining spaces.Sean Payton purchased the Belcaro mansion for $4.55 million in March 2023. In June 2026, he signed a five-year deal with the Denver Broncos which is in the neighborhood of $18 million per year, as per NBC Sports’ Peter King.As per The Denver Post, Sean Payton’s Belcaro mansion was developed by Raymond Development Group. The gated property features a modern architectural design across two levels.The upscale residence is defined by generous proportions. The main level has 11-foot ceilings.White oak-flooring is laid in a herringbone pattern, thereby adding a refined touch to the living rooms. The mansion’s open layout allows living and entertaining areas to blend into one another, thereby creating a spacious environment throughout the property.The kitchen is what stands out in the mansion. The oversized kitchen features a large central island which acts as an additional preparation space and a gathering spot.A glass wine wall offers a luxury element to the kitchen. The dedicated display and storage area can accommodate hundreds of bottles, thereby offering the kitchen and surrounding entertaining spaces a stunning visual allure.When an oversized kitchen, high ceilings, and custom flooring combine, it offers the upscale residence a polished contemporary character without entirely relying on its square footage.The Belcaro mansion also includes several features designed for quiet privacy and accommodating convenience. The primary suite has its own fireplace and dual closets, thereby creating a comfortable retreat within the two-story mansion.An elevator in the home connects the levels, thereby giving practical luxury features to the detached, single-family luxury home within a gated community.As per New Orleans Luxury Living’s Elizabeth McNulty, Sean Payton owned a magnificent Greek Revival mansion in New Orleans while he coached the New Orleans Saints. The property was situated in the best part of Uptown, on an exceptionally rare and oversized corner lot. He won a Super Bowl for them in a victory over the Indianapolis Colts for the 2009 season. Article Title: Sidney Crosby spent decades at the centre of NHL history: Inside the private family life behind the Pittsburgh Penguins icon, from his parents to his sister and upbringing in Nova Scotia
Article Text:
Sidney Crosby of the Pittsburgh Penguins looks on against the Carolina Hurricanes (Credit: Getty Images)

Sidney Crosby’s family shaped his remarkable NHL journey

Sidney Crosby’s early hockey development began at home

Troy Crosby and Trina Crosby supported Sidney

Taylor Crosby shares the family’s hockey connection

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Sidney Crosby has had a phenomenal NHL career that has made him one of the most recognisable figures in hockey, but the story off the ice has been much more private. Crosby is a gifted young player who grew up in Cole Harbour, Nova Scotia, in a close-knit family that was influential in shaping his approach to hockey and life before he became the captain of the Pittsburgh Penguins.His parents, Troy and Trina Crosby, played a big part in his early years, and his younger sister, Taylor Crosby, grew her own affinity for the game. The family as a whole provided a grounding influence as Sidney moved from a highly regarded local prospect to an NHL superstar.Sidney Crosby was born on August 7, 1987, in Cole Harbour, Nova Scotia, a community just outside of Halifax that remains synonymous with his identity. His early years were spent in a relatively modest family, a far cry from the attention that would eventually surround his hockey career. The Pittsburgh Penguins have referred to the Crosby household as one of hard work, humility and strong ties to the local community.That environment became especially important as Crosby’s hockey ability began to outpace other players his age. He was skating from a young age and started in organised hockey as a kid.By the time he was a mere teenager, his playing was being noticed far beyond the borders of Nova Scotia. According to NHL.com, his father, Troy, put him on skates before he was three years old and helped teach him the fundamentals of the game.In those early years, Troy Crosby was more than just Sidney’s father; he was an important hockey influence as well. Troy, a former goalie, was drafted by the Montreal Canadiens in the 12th round of the 1984 NHL Draft. Although he never played in the NHL, he knew the game well enough from his playing days to help guide his son's development.Sidney was making remarkable rapid progress. He would play with older kids, and he always had skills that were far beyond his age group. At seven, he was already at a hockey school in Halifax for the best young players from the Maritimes. Eventually, his development took him away from home for opportunities to accelerate his path toward professional hockey.Troy Crosby’s influence in Sidney’s development as a hockey player is well documented, but Trina Crosby’s role in the family environment that surrounded the future NHL captain was equally important. The couple raised Sidney and Taylor in Cole Harbour, focusing on the values that would keep their children grounded as their sporting ambitions grew.A stable family environment was particularly valuable for Sidney in the face of growing attention. His rise through junior hockey was met with huge expectations, and his arrival with the Pittsburgh Penguins only put him under an even bigger spotlight. But the family was also a link to the life he had lived before the fame of the professional world.Troy and Trina have also been there for important moments along their son’s career. Crosby netted his 600th NHL goal in November of 2024, and both parents were on hand at PPG Paints Arena to witness the milestone in person. Later, Crosby said it meant so much to have his family there for such a big accomplishment.Privacy has become one of the defining characteristics of Crosby's public persona. His professional achievements have been well documented, but details of his personal life have been comparatively scant.Sidney’s little sister Taylor Crosby carved her own path in hockey. Taylor, eight years younger than her brother, eventually became a goaltender who played through competitive hockey programs, providing another strong bond between the Crosby family and the game.Taylor didn’t take up hockey at an extremely young age as Sidney did. She began around 10 o’clock, when Sidney was already out of town, chasing his junior career, Hockey Canada reported. Then she went to Shattuck-St. Mary’s, the same Minnesota prep school her brother played at before.Growing up with Sidney Crosby as her brother meant living with one of the sport’s biggest names, but Taylor’s own hockey journey unfolded on its own. She played at the prep level and then went on to further her education and hockey career at the collegiate level.Her relationship with Sidney, too, was distinctly a sibling affair. While they were home together and she was getting ready to go to school, Sidney kept shooting pucks at Taylor, Hockey Canada said. Taylor joked that as she improved, she was starting to block more of his shots.Sidney's job has taken him all over North America and the world, but the family has remained connected to Cole Harbour. His parents still live in the family home linked to his childhood that remains in the city, the Penguins have said.That hometown connection has translated to Crosby’s charitable work, as well. He has helped youth sports and charitable causes in Nova Scotia through his Sidney Crosby Foundation, including assisting kids looking for opportunities to get involved in sports. He has also been linked to a hockey school in Cole Harbour that has welcomed young players from other parts of the world.The result is a family saga that is not your typical celebrity story. Crosby’s career has delivered championships, international success and historic milestones, but those closest to him have generally stayed out of the constant glare of professional sports.From the influence of Troy and Trina when he was growing up to Taylor’s own hockey journey, Crosby’s family has kept him connected to the life he had before the NHL spotlight. His career may have taken him far beyond Nova Scotia, but the values of his Cole Harbour upbringing have continued to be an important part of the Sidney Crosby story.
Article Summary: Sidney Crosby grew up in Cole Harbour, Nova Scotia, in a close-knit family. His parents, Troy and Trina, were influential in shaping his approach to hockey and life before he became the captain of the Pittsburgh Penguins. Sidney’s little sister, Taylor, carved her own path in hockey. The family as a whole provided a grounding influence as Sidney moved from a highly regarded local prospect to an NHL superstar.

Former India cricketer Suresh Raina believes Mohammed Shami could soon return to the national team, following the comeback of his former teammate Bhuvneshwar Kumar, who has earned a recall at the age of 36.Raina credited Bhuvneshwar’s discipline, hard work and commitment to his fitness for his return to the Indian side, expressing confidence that Shami could also be back in contention after making an impact in domestic cricket.“Making it to the Indian team at the age of 36 shows character. He has been a very disciplined bowler and a very process-driven guy who has worked really hard on his body," Raina said while speaking at the jersey launch of the Indian Soft Ball Cricket League.Raina was equally optimistic about Shami’s prospects, pointing to his performances in domestic cricket and suggesting that a return to the national team could be around the corner.“Absolutely, I think he (Mohammed Shami) has done well and played good domestic cricket too. Now it is Bhuvi’s turn, aur Shami bhi aa rahe hai piche piche, tension mat lijiye (Shami is also right behind him, so don’t worry)," Raina added.Shami last featured for India during the 2025 Champions Trophy, while his most recent appearance in Test cricket came in the 2023 World Test Championship final against Australia. Since then, the fast bowler has continued to play domestic cricket and is set to represent Bengal in their opening fixture of the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season.However, his recent IPL numbers have been a concern. Shami has managed just 18 wickets in 22 matches across the 2025 and 2026 seasons, conceding runs at an economy rate of 10 per over.Bhuvneshwar, meanwhile, has demonstrated how skill and precision can compensate for a lack of outright pace in the shortest format. Although his gentle pace might appear to put him at a disadvantage, particularly on flat pitches, his ability to swing the new ball and execute variations at the death has helped him remain effective.The right-arm pacer was particularly effective in the PowerPlay and death overs, claiming 25 wickets in overs 1-6 and another 18 in overs 16-20 across the 2025 and 2026 IPL seasons.Bhuvneshwar took his game to another level in IPL 2026, finishing as the second-highest wicket-taker with 28 scalps at an economy rate of 8.07. He was one of the key figures in Royal Challengers Bengaluru’s title-winning campaign, helping the franchise secure back-to-back titles.Those figures put Bhuvneshwar ahead of Josh Hazlewood, Jofra Archer and Mohammed Siraj in the two key phases of the innings, underlining the value of his control and experience.His return to the Indian team has also offered a reminder that sustained discipline and an understanding of a bowler’s role can keep the door open to international cricket. Kalyani: Bengal return to their cricket academy ground in Kalyani, where their Ranji Trophy dream came crashing down in February, hoping to make a fresh start when they take on Delhi in their opening match of the new season on Sunday.Bengal suffered a semifinal defeat to eventual champions Jammu & Kashmir despite securing a first-innings lead last season. This time, they will look to turn the page at the same venue, with history offering an added incentive. Bengal’s last Ranji Trophy triumph came in 1989-90, when they defeated Delhi in the final.Delhi, meanwhile, have turned to Vijay Dahiya , reappointing the former India wicketkeeper as coach ahead of the campaign. Dahiya had guided Delhi to their last title in 2007-08 and will hope to revive a side that has struggled to progress beyond the group stage in recent seasons.“Nothing happens overnight. I am here to see the team is moving in the right direction,” Dahiya told TOI.Bengal will look to make a strong start, especially as they will be without their star pacers Akash Deep and Mukesh Kumar , who have been picked for the ‘A’ side for the New Zealand tour from the next match.Dahiya gave full respect to Bengal’s star pace duo, who will be joined by another experienced pacer in Mohammed Shami.After spending eight months on the sidelines with a lower-back stress injury, Akash Deep returned with a match haul of 6/68 to help Rest of India beat J&K in the Irani Cup. Akash Deep believes he has regained his rhythm and pace.“I am my own competitor. I am not worried about what the other bowlers are doing. You can never play cricket thinking about who will replace you. What I can do is produce a better version of myself and I am fully focused on doing that,” he said.

Article Title: Ranji Trophy returns with Jaiswal, Rahul, Jadeja in action as India’s Test stars turn to domestic cricket

In the age of the IPL and expanding state T20 leagues, the Ranji Trophy remains Indian cricket ’s most prestigious red-ball tournament. Its 92nd edition begins on Sunday, with 37 teams in action in the opening round. Arunachal Pradesh will miss the first round, taking the number to 38 from the next round.The start of the season will have added star power, with Yashasvi Jaiswal turning out for Mumbai, KL Rahul for Karnataka and Washington Sundar for Tamil Nadu before they leave for the India ‘A’ shadow tour of New Zealand. Veteran allrounder Ravindra Jadeja will also be in action for Saurashtra. With India scheduled to play seven Tests over the next four months, two in New Zealand and five at home against Australia, the tournament carries extra significance for domestic performers hoping to push their case.Recent selections have shown that Ranji Trophy performances are being rewarded. Jammu & Kashmir swing bowler Auqib Nabi, who took 60 wickets in 10 matches last season, earned an India call-up. Left-arm spinner Manav Suthar, Devdutt Padikkal, off-spinner Saransh Jain and Karnataka batter Ravichandran Smaran have also benefited from strong domestic returns.BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia said the Ranji Trophy remains central to India’s talent pathway.“The Ranji Trophy is the premier domestic cricket tournament in India. All players who want to make a mark nationally and internationally have to take this tournament seriously because all eyes are on performances here,” Saikia told TOI.Saikia reiterated the BCCI’s policy that all available India players must play domestic cricket. “Whoever is available and not on national duty is mandatorily required to participate in the Ranji Trophy or other domestic tournaments,” he said. “It keeps senior players in rhythm and helps youngsters learn by sharing the dressing room with them.”

Article Title: ‘Their careers are on the line too’: Gautam Gambhir’s blunt message after India’s bowling struggles
Article Text:
Gautam Gambhir

Bat-ball imbalance irks coach again

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Dube promotion fails to make an impact

Ranchi: Roston Chase ’s miserly spell of 3/24 in four overs was crucial in a run-fest in which 501 runs were scored in 38.3 overs, as West Indies stunned India by six wickets in the second T20I. On a surface that produced 249/5 for India and 252/4 for West Indies, Chase stood out with his ability to read the conditions and constantly change his lines. He removed three of India’s first four batters, briefly checking the hosts’ momentum before India recovered through their middle order.India head coach Gautam Gambhir highlighted Chase’s adaptability as the key to his success. “The way he altered his lines was very important because, on this wicket, changing your line matters a lot. Length may or may not change, but if you keep changing the line, you keep the batter guessing,” Gambhir said. “He bowled at the feet, went wide and bowled full. He kept mixing it up. On a wicket like this, that variation is extremely important.”The contrast was stark in the second innings. Express quick Mayank Yadav struck twice in the opening over as West Indies were reduced to 5/2 and then lost a third wicket in the Powerplay. But Shai Hope and Sherfane Rutherford turned the game around with a 120-run fourth-wicket stand off 54 balls. Hope finished unbeaten on a hundred, while Rutherford smashed 84 off 37 balls.Gambhir admitted the conditions made life difficult for the bowlers but insisted India could not use that as an excuse. “These are tough conditions for bowling. We know that flat wickets with dew make things difficult, but we need to figure out a way to stop the opposition,” he said.In a contest dominated by batting, Chase’s ability to remain economical and keep changing his angles provided a reminder that even on a belter, intelligent bowling can still influence the outcome. His 3/24 was not merely the best spell of the night; it was the spell that briefly brought control to a game otherwise almost entirely dictated by the bat.The defeat also brought Gambhir’s growing concern over the imbalance between bat and ball into focus. After India chased down a 400-plus target in fewer than 44 overs in the Guwahati ODI last week, he had said, “This is not cricket, this is batting.”In Ranchi, his assessment was along similar lines. “If you want an even contest, we want that too,” he said, adding, “Those bowlers are our bowlers. Their careers are on the line too. An even contest would make for better cricket.”The coach also defended the decision to promote Shivam Dube to No. 4, insisting it was part of a long-term strategy rather than a one-off move. Dube could manage only seven off 10 deliveries.“We’ve used him in that role for a long period, including before and during the World Cup. Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn’t,” he said.
Article Summary: West Indies beat India by six wickets in second T20I in Ranchi. Roston Chase takes 3/24 in four overs. Shai Hope and Sherfane Rutherford add 120-run fourth- wicket stand. Gautam Gambhir defends Shivam Dube's promotion to No. 4.

Article Title: Shubhankar Sharma's six-shot victory at Kapil Dev Invitational provides timely boost ahead of PGTI Championship
Article Text:
Shubhankar Sharma

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Shubhankar Sharma could hardly have asked for better preparation ahead of the PGTI Championship. The Chandigarh golfer produced a composed final-round performance to win the Kapil Dev Invitational Tour Championship by six strokes at Jaypee Greens Golf & Spa Resort on Sunday, finishing with a three-under 69 for a total of 14-under 274.Starting the day with a two-shot lead, Sharma faced a stern challenge from Italy’s Michele Ortolani before pulling away in the closing holes. The victory was his second in as many appearances on the Professional Golf Tour of India (PGTI) this season, underlining the form he has been building in recent months.For Sharma, the win meant more than another trophy. After going eight years without a professional title, he broke that drought at the Boulders Classic in April. His latest triumph suggests that the confidence gained there is beginning to translate into consistent performances.With the PGTI Championship scheduled at Delhi Golf Club from Oct 15 to 18, the timing could hardly be better. The event will bring together some of the biggest names in world golf, and Sharma will head into the week with renewed belief in his game.“I won; I'm very happy. It wasn't a very good last week. My main goal coming here was to find momentum,” Sharma said after the victory.“It's a very technical game where you sometimes have to go back to your basics.”Sharma arrived at the venue on Monday and spent much of his preparation working on the fundamentals. That effort paid off over the four rounds, although the final day was far from straightforward.He began with a couple of early birdies, but bogeys midway through the round allowed Ortolani to narrow the gap. A dropped shot on the 10th added to the pressure and briefly threatened to make the contest more complicated than Sharma would have liked.“I expected the lead to narrow unless I made a very fast start. I made two early birdies, but I wasn't playing my best. Michele played extremely well, and then I made a poor bogey on the 10th. That was probably my worst shot of the day,” he said.The turning point came on the par-five 12th. Playing in gusty conditions, Sharma sank a putt from around 60 to 70 feet for an eagle, restoring his advantage at a crucial stage of the round. It was the kind of shot that changed the mood of the contest and gave him the breathing space he needed.Although the final margin was six strokes, Sharma still had work to do before he could celebrate. His short game came under pressure on the closing stretch, particularly on the 16th, where a wayward tee shot was blown behind a tree. Faced with a difficult recovery from a bare lie, he had to rely on his touch to save Par.“The greens were very hard and fast, so it wasn't easy. Putting was definitely a challenge,” Sharma explained. “If you miss the fairway, to stop it on the green becomes really hard because the rough comes between the ball and the club and you can't impart as much spin as you want on the ball.”Having last played at Jaypee Greens in 2013, Sharma was familiar with the venue but found plenty to test him, particularly with the demanding pin positions.That preparation will now be put to the test against a formidable international field at the India Championship. Defending champion Tommy Fleetwood will be joined by two-time Masters winner Rory McIlroy, reigning Open champion Ryan Fox, and former Masters champions Patrick Reed and Bubba Watson, among other leading players from the PGA Tour and European Tour.Sharma's experience on the international circuit could prove valuable. A two-time European Tour winner, he has spent much of the past nine years competing overseas and is accustomed to the depth of competition at that level.“Obviously, the experience of the European Tour is great for me,” he said. “I've been there for nine years, so I rarely come back and play.”He also credited Roundglass and the Roundglass Foundation for supporting his career and giving him the opportunity to compete regularly abroad. That backing, he said, has played an important role in his development as a golfer.Returning to India, however, brings its own advantages. Beyond the familiar courses, Sharma values the friendships and sense of belonging he finds on the domestic circuit, where he first developed as a professional.Sharma also sees room for Indian golf to grow, particularly through the development of more challenging courses and greater opportunities to compete against international players. While he recognises the quality of courses already available in the country, he believes comparisons with overseas venues need to account for differences in climate, grass types, and course design.There was encouragement for the domestic circuit elsewhere in the leaderboard, too. Bengaluru's Manoj S finished tied for second with Ortolani at eight-under 280. His runner-up finish lifted him from 26th to 17th in the Race to India Championship, securing his place in next week's field.Khalin Joshi finished fourth at seven-under, while Harman Sachdeva and Yuvraj Sandhu shared fifth place at six-under.Saptak Talwar continued to lead the season-long race, with Viraj Madappa occupying the final qualifying position through the current PGTI Order of Merit.For Sharma his week at Jaypee Greens delivered exactly what he had come looking for, a return to form, greater confidence, and a timely reminder of what he can achieve when his game comes together.The next step will be turning that momentum into a strong showing on home soil against an elite international field.
Article Summary: Shubhankar Sharma wins Kapil Dev Invitational Tour Championship by six strokes. The Chandigarh golfer finished with a three-under 69 for a total of 14-under 274. The victory was his second in as many appearances on the Professional Golf Tour of India (PGTI) this season.

Their fielding has also been a concern, with the team recording the most dropped catches among Full Member sides in T20Is since the start of 2025, alongside high numbers of misfields and missed run-out opportunities.On surfaces where boundaries come easily, such lapses can prove costly.India's bowling numbers, however, point to one particularly important factor. Bumrah's presence gives the attack a level of effectiveness that has been difficult to replicate in his absence. As India look to regain control of the T20I series, the contrast in results with and without their premier fast bowler offers a clear indication of just how central he is to the team's bowling strength.
