Article Title: Mask and Face must face same consequences: SC stays HC bail, sends Rs 3,000 crore drug case accused to jail
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: “Mask must face the same consequences as the Face”, “If your masters are in jail, you will serve them better by being there, not outside” – were the caustic remarks by Supreme Court on Thursday as it send back to prison an accused who was granted bail by the Punjab and Haryana HC in a huge narcotic drug trafficking case.The case related to seizure of 5,000 tablets of tramadol from one Ashu Arora last February in Amritsar and subsequent unearthing of an inter-state illegal drug trafficking syndicate. Senior advocate Maninder Singh, appearing for the accused, argued that HC had granted bail six months ago putting a premium on the liberty of citizens and because of his illegal custody.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked, given the gravity of the crime, a Rs 3,000 crore illegal drug trafficking syndicate and seizure of 5,000 Tramadol tablets, can the illegal detention prior to arrest vitiate the arrest itself as has been cited by the HC?When Singh said that his client, Anuj Kumar Singh, was a mere employee of those who were allegedly running the inter-state drug trafficking network, the bench said, “You are a ‘mukhota’ (mask) which was as much involved in the crime as the face itself.”“When your masters are in jail, you can serve them better by being there with them, not outside,” the bench said while expressing serious concern over the menace of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances in the state. The senior advocate said that there was no evidence of any seizure of drugs from his client.The bench said, “In a game of football, there are 11 players but all of them do not have possession of the ball simultaneously.”The counsel said his client was not even a 12th player. Switching to cricket from football, the bench said, “He was either a cover or an extra-cover.”The bench said it would cancel the bail, ask the prosecution to complete the trial in one year and if it does not complete, then the accused can apply for regular bail. When Singh protested saying the accused had cooperated with the investigation and regularly attended trial while being on bail, the bench said, “For a Rs 3,000 crore drug trafficking case, one year in jail is nothing.”It asked the accused to surrender within two weeks and asked him to respond to the Union govt’s appeal against HC order granting bail.When Singh cited the HC’s decision to grant bail because of illegal custody prior to arrest and the premium it put on liberty, the bench said, “We also continuously ruled in favour of preserving liberty if there are other redeeming features. In your case, we do not find your cooperation in investigation or attendance of trial in the face of nature of crime and the restrictions in law to be a very relevant redeeming feature. Your arguments are most persuasive. In any other case we would have agreed with you.”
Article Summary: The case related to seizure of 5,000 tablets of tramadol from one Ashu Arora last February in Amritsar. Senior advocate Maninder Singh, appearing for the accused, argued that HC had granted bail six months ago putting a premium on liberty of citizens.

Article Title: ‘Serving a hungry lion a goat on a platter’: Ashwin explains how Shai Hope helped Sanju Samson regain form
Article Text:
India's Sanju Samson (PTI Photo)

Former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin has questioned Shai Hope ’s bowling decisions during the second T20I against India, arguing that the West Indies captain made a tactical error by persisting with Akeal Hosein despite the spinner being taken apart by Sanju Samson India piled up 249/5 in 20 overs in Ranchi on Friday, with Samson smashing 82 off just 41 deliveries. West Indies, however, produced a stunning response with the bat, chasing down the target with nine balls to spare as Hope struck an unbeaten 102 off 45 balls to level the five-match series at 1-1.While India’s batting dominated the first half of the contest, Ashwin felt Hope missed an opportunity to contain Samson by continuing to use Hosein during the PowerPlay.The left-arm spinner conceded 46 runs in three overs, struggling to contain Samson, who punished him with two sixes and two fours in one over. Despite the batter’s aggressive approach, Hope gave Hosein three consecutive overs before eventually leaving him out of the attack for the remainder of the innings.Ashwin criticised the decision, saying the West Indies captain could not expect to build pressure by repeatedly using a spinner against a batter who was finding boundaries with ease.“Samson looked scratchy because he was not in a run-scoring phase. However, Shai Hope also made a mistake today. You cannot keep using spinners from one end in an attempt to build pressure on Sanju Samson. Bowling three consecutive overs from Akeal Hosein during the powerplay was like serving a hungry lion a goat on a platter. Samson simply took advantage of the opportunity and went after Akeal Hosein," said Ashwin on his YouTube channel, Ash Ki Baat.Ashwin also praised Samson's approach, highlighting his willingness to keep taking risks for the team despite the pressure surrounding his place in the side."It is not easy to maintain that attitude. It is human nature that when you are in danger and know that you might be dropped, self-preservation becomes the top priority. Yet, he continues to take risks for the team. And it is this great attitude of his that seems to be bringing him some luck as well. A catch went straight into a fielder's hands today, but he dropped it," he added.Despite the expensive spell, West Indies managed to turn the game around with a commanding batting display. Hope led the chase with an unbeaten century, helping the visitors overcome the pressure of pursuing a total close to 250. West Indies also showed resilience by completing the chase despite losing three wickets inside the first six overs.The result has added to the growing debate around the balance between bat and ball in the series. India and West Indies have both produced high-scoring performances, with batting-friendly conditions making life difficult for the bowlers.India will now look to address their difficulties in defending big totals, with head coach Gautam Gambhir having stressed the need for a better balance between bat and ball. The teams head to Indore for the next contest, where another high-scoring encounter could await.
Article Summary: Ravichandran Ashwin criticises West Indies captain Shai Hope. Ashwin says Hope made a tactical error by continuing to use Akeal Hosein during the PowerPlay. India piled up 249/5 in 20 overs, with Sanju Samson scoring 82. West Indies produced a stunning response with the bat, chasing down the target with nine balls to spare.

Article Title: Palliative care is not simply for end-of-life patients, say practitioners
Article Text:
Palliative care is not only about treatment and therapy, but holistic wellbeing.





In two adjoining rooms at the Romila Palliative Care centre, off Pali Naka in Bandra, sit Ibrahim Syed, a 33-year-old man, and Roohi Salamsheikh, a 47-year-old woman. One has had a stroke; the other has been the caregiver of someone who has.Both might seem unlikely recipients of palliative care, which is associated almost exclusively with terminal illness, and invariably, with cancer. Practitioners of this system of healthcare are working hard to change that perception—an effort that was doubled on Saturday’s World Hospice and Palliative Care Day, with awareness programmes conducted nationwide."There is a misunderstanding that palliative care is only about end-of-life care, but the truth is that it is needed for any life-limiting or life-threatening illness," says Jerry Pinto, whose 2025 book A Good Life: The Power of Palliative Care describes standout models of care across the country. "Diabetes is a life-limiting illness, so is Parkinson's Disease. The awareness that these patients and their caregivers need palliation too is not widespread in society. "According to a recent study in the journal ecancermedicalscience, India has just four palliative care centres for every 10 million people.Palliative care works in tandem with medical treatment to reduce pain, control symptoms and minimise distress from serious illness.It's a holistic approach that encompasses the psychological and financial aspects of life-limiting conditions. So a palliative care team is typically multidisciplinary, consisting not just of doctors and physiotherapists but also psychologists, occupational therapists and medical social workers."Long drawn-out chronic illnesses drain patients and caregivers of everything, including finances," says cardiologist Dr. Eric Borges. "Palliative care attempts to ease all incumbent pressures, so that the patient responds better to treatment and improves their quality of life."Dr. Borges is the founder of Sukoon Nilaya (Abode of Tranquility), a 35-bed, free palliative care facility run by the King George V Memorial Trust at Mahalaxmi. Funded by Cipla Foundation, Tata Trusts and others, it is Mumbai's only in-patient palliative care facility that prioritizes non-cancer patients, including children.“I initially had a tough time convincing colleagues that non-cancer patients needed help too," Dr. Borges says, “Awareness of the need for palliative care for non-cancer patients has only emerged in the last 10 years.”At Sukoon Nilaya, patients are admitted for at least 15 days and stay as long as rehabilitation requires. Every patient must be accompanied by a caregiver, who is taught how to look after them at home and must pass a caregiver test before they’re discharged.“We were taught how to exercise, bathe and feed Heba," says Mirza Abu Wafa, whose 13-year-old daughter, who has Down’s Syndrome, suffered a serious neck injury and was on a ventilator for five months at Wadia Hospital. “We were told she would never survive without a ventilator. But at Sukoon Nilaya, she was off it in 13 days,” says Mirza, who gave up his job on a goat farm to care for his daughter and borrowed money for her medical expenses. “I spent Rs 15 lakhs at Wadia. And zero at Sukoon Nilaya, where we spent two months.”The brief often goes beyond conventional healthcare. “A family may need food rations, educational assistance or even a means of livelihood,” says Anita Bansode, a medical social worker at Sukoon Nilaya, who recently helped a patient’s father, a tailor, obtain a sewing machine through an NGO.Roohi Salamsheikh and her husband Abdul had never heard of palliative care until they came by a pamphlet at Cooper Hospital. They got in touch with Romila Palliative Care (RPC) for help with Roohi’s mother, who suffered a stroke in 2021. As the primary caregiver, Roohi developed severe backache tending her bed-ridden mother in her small Jogeshwari rental. "I grew weak and depressed,” she says, describing caregiver burnout. Relief came with RPC through free medicines and diapers, monthly doctor visits—and crucially, a helpline.“Palliative care views the family as a unit of care,” says Dr Bhavika Hotchandani, Program Director at Romila Palliative Care, part of the nonprofit SNEHA, whose model constitutes home-based care, outpatient clinics in government hospitals and community outreach, including awareness camps and doorstep drives in vulnerable neighbourhoods of Dharavi and Andheri. They support approximately 1,700 patients a year, free of cost.Dr. Hotchandani says their work is structured across three pillars: caregiver empowerment, with practical training in duties like bed mobility and wound dressing; psychosocial and bereavement support; and navigational support, where families are assisted in figuring out referrals to specialists, hospitals, and other services.SNEHA’s model includes home-based care, outpatient clinics in government hospitals and community outreach, including in vulnerable neighbourhoods. They support approximately 1,700 patients a year, free of cost. In 2022, it entered a public-private partnership with the BMC to run palliative care OPDs in government hospitals.The government knows palliative care matters but has been slow to act. The National Programme for Palliative Care was launched by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in 2012, but it remains on paper. However, practitioners in the state see hope in plans announced by Mah’s health department earlier this year to set up palliative care centres and home-based care in every district.Home care is the most important part, says Dr. Geeta Joshi, President of the Indian Association of Palliative Care. "Palliative care is the only specialty where you have to go to the home of the patient. And so, it’s vital to integrate hospital-based services with community-level services," she says, adding that private hospitals are loath to do so due to lack of revenue.There’s little uptake by practitioners too, because it's neither lucrative nor attractive, says Dr. Prakash Fernandes, Head - Palliative Care Partnerships, Cipla Foundation, which runs the Cipla Palliative Care & Training Centre in Pune. “An attitude change is needed, where palliative care is not viewed as ‘good to do’, but as an essential part of regular healthcare. It should be integrated into the MBBS curriculum,” he recommends.Eventually, it's only the gov that can drive palliative care at scale, says Dr. Borges—and it's people who should demand it.
Article Summary: World Hospice and Palliative Care Day was held on Saturday. India has just four palliative care centres for every 10 million people. The awareness that these patients and their caregivers need palliation too is not widespread in society. The holistic approach encompasses the psychological and financial aspects of life-limiting conditions.

Article Title: “India, you’ve come a long way”: Foreign traveller returns after 17 years and is amazed by the country’s changing roads
Article Text:
Road trip to Delhi (@stayingboundless/Instagram)

The video

Her latest drive left her impressed

The interesting caption

India's expanding highway network

Rest stops are an important part of road travel

What makes the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway significant?

Projects like the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway, the Delhi-Amritsar-Katra Corridor, and the Amritsar-Jamnagar Economic Corridor are set to completely redefine cross-country logistics.

It’s a fact that in India, a road trip can be an adventure in itself. However, for one foreign traveller, the roads of India have changed dramatically over the past 17 years. The woman returned to India nearly after two decades and was left amazed with the present road conditions. She drove from Jaipur to Delhi via expressway and was surprised by the transformation. From smoother highways to clean toilets and proper rest stops, she experienced everything a road trip can offer.Known as @stayingboundless, she shared her experience on Instagram. The woman recalled how road trips in India once filled her with fear. Bad roads, hours of being tossed around in a vehicle and the lack of clean washrooms made long journeys challenging. She even remembered having to plan her water intake around the availability of bathrooms.“This week I drove from Jaipur to Delhi on the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway and honestly couldn’t believe it,” she wrote on her Insta post describing the road as smooth and open, with proper rest stops and clean bathrooms. Calling it one of the most impressive changes she had seen in India, she invited other travellers to share their experiences too.“Seventeen years ago, a road trip in India filled me with dread. Rough roads, hours of bouncing around, and almost no clean places to stop. You planned your water intake around the bathrooms, or the lack of them. This week I drove from Jaipur to Delhi on the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway and honestly couldn’t believe it. Smooth, open road, real rest stops, clean bathrooms and decent coffee. It’s one of the most impressive changes I’ve seen in India. Have you driven it yet? Tell me what you think in the comments.”The traveller's experience comes against the backdrop of a substantial expansion of India's road infrastructure over the past decade. According to the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways' Annual Report 2024-25, India's National Highway network grew from 91,287 km in 2014 to 1,46,195 km. The expressways are designed for faster movement with controlled entry and exit points.One of the most impressive features of the traveller's account is her appreciation of facilities that are often overlooked. Clean toilets and reliable places to take a break may seem like small conveniences, but they can influence whether people feel comfortable undertaking a long road journey.The government’s aim is to offer travellers with more organised places to stop rather than having to depend entirely on whatever facilities happen to be available along a route. For families with young children, elderly passengers and people travelling long distances, this can be particularly valuable.The Delhi-Mumbai Expressway is among India's major highway infrastructure projects. Planned as a 1,386-km corridor, it is designed to connect the Delhi region with Haryana, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Maharashtra, improving links between important economic centres. The expressway is intended to improve connectivity and reduce travel time, although the actual journey depends on the operational stretch, traffic conditions, entry and exit points, and the route taken.For the woman returning to India after 17 years, however, the difference was not simply a matter of kilometres or minutes. It was the experience of travelling on a modern highway with facilities that made the drive feel more convenient.She ended her post with a simple reaction that summed up her surprise: “India, you’ve come a long way.”
Article Summary: The Delhi-Mumbai Expressway is among India's major highway infrastructure projects. The 1,386-km corridor is designed to connect the Delhi region with Haryana, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Maharashtra. It is intended to improve connectivity and reduce travel time.

Article Title: Sobhana Mostary scripts history, becomes first Bangladesh woman to score century against Australia
Article Text:
Sobhana Mostary (Image: IANS)

Mostary, Sultana rescue Bangladesh after early collapse

Record-breaking partnership rewrites ODI history

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bangladesh aim to level the series

Sobhana Mostary produced a record-breaking performance as Bangladesh recovered from a disastrous start to post 220/6 against Australia in the second ODI at Allan Border Field. The right-handed batter struck her maiden international century, becoming the first Bangladesh woman to score an international hundred against Australia.Mostary's 118 off 134 balls proved crucial for the visitors after Australia elected to bowl first in the must-win encounter. Her fighting knock, combined with a valuable contribution from captain Nigar Sultana , helped Bangladesh recover from 8/3 and give themselves a competitive total.Bangladesh were in deep trouble early in their innings, losing three wickets for just eight runs. However, Mostary and Sultana joined forces to turn the game around, stitching together a remarkable 195-run partnership for the fourth wicket.Mostary showcased composure and determination throughout her innings, striking 18 boundaries to bring up a memorable century. Sultana provided equally important support, scoring 74 off 114 deliveries as the pair steadied the innings and laid the foundation for Bangladesh's recovery.Before Mostary's century, Sultana held the record for the highest individual score by a Bangladesh woman against Australia, having scored an unbeaten 63 in a T20I.The 195-run stand between Mostary and Sultana became Bangladesh's highest partnership for any wicket in women's ODI cricket. The duo surpassed the previous record of 152 runs, which Sultana and Sharmin Akhter had registered for the third wicket against Thailand in 2025.The partnership also established a new benchmark against Australia in women's ODIs, eclipsing the previous record of 170 runs. New Zealand's Emily Drumm and Rebecca Rolls had held that record with their second-wicket stand in 2002.Mostary's landmark innings ended in the 48th over when Megan Schutt bowled her for 118. Schutt finished with four wickets, having struck twice in the powerplay to dismiss Fargana Hoque and Sharmin Akhter before later removing Shorna Akter.Despite the early setbacks, Bangladesh showed resilience to finish at 220/6, with Mostary and Sultana's record partnership providing the backbone of their innings. The visitors entered the second ODI looking to bounce back after losing the series opener.
Article Summary: Sobhana Mostary scores maiden international century against Australia. Mostary and Nigar Sultana stitch together 195-run partnership for fourth wicket. Bangladesh recover from 8/3 to post 220/6 in second ODI at Allan Border Field.

Article Title: Abhijeet Dipke’s mother: ‘Why is govt detaining him when it is not arresting rapists?’
Article Text:
For the Dipke family, Saturday became a day marked by both political confrontation and personal loss.





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Barely hours after CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke was detained by Delhi police upon landing in the national capital on Saturday morning, his grandmother died at the family home in Maharashtra’s Hingoli district. The Dipke family is not sure if he will be allowed to attend her last rites on Sunday.The double blow triggered an emotional response from Dipke’s family members, who accused govt of targeting him and demanded answers over his detention.“My mother, Savitribai, breathed her last around 12.30pm at our home in Santuk Pimpri village. She was unwell and bedridden for some time. Abhijeet and she shared a close bond,” said Bhagwanrao Dipke, the CJP founder’s father.“Since his illegal detention, we have not been able to speak to him and we don’t know his whereabouts. We don’t know whether he will be returning to attend his grandmother’s last rites on Sunday morning,” he added. As he travelled to Hingoli to attend his mother’s funeral, Bhagwanrao questioned the police action. He demanded that Delhi Police disclose the legal grounds for detaining his son and asked what offence he had committed.Despite the detention, Bhagwanrao said the family would stand by his son. “I am not worried about Abhijeet. He has chosen to take up this cause, and we will stand by him.”Dipke’s mother, Anita, also lashed out at govt. “Why is govt detaining Abhijeet when it is not arresting rapists? They (police personnel) went into the aircraft to detain him. What kind of rule is this?” she asked.Recalling a conversation before one of his trips, she said she had warned her son that he could be detained at any time. “He told me, ‘Mummy, it is not like that. I want to do something for the country. I belong to this country’,” she said. Dipke had declared before reaching Delhi that he was prepared to face arrest.For the Dipke family, Saturday became a day marked by both political confrontation and personal loss. Even as they prepare for her last rites, the uncertainty over if Abhijeet Dipke will be allowed to bid a final farewell to his grandmother now hangs over the family members.
Article Summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke was detained by Delhi police upon landing in the national capital on Saturday morning. Hours later, his grandmother died at the family home in Maharashtra’s Hingoli district. The Dipke family is not sure if he will be allowed to attend her last rites on Sunday.

Article Title: Satara police arrest three in jewellery shop theft, recover Rs9.15 lakh stolen goods
Article Text:
Kolhapur:





The Satara city police have arrested three suspects, including a minor, for allegedly breaking open the shutter of a jewellery shop at Shete Chowk in Satara and stealing goods worth Rs9.15 lakh. The theft took place on the night of Oct 7.The three suspects, all from Satara, were apprehended following a police investigation into the incident after Akshay Ankush Shinde (31), a resident of Patkhal, filed a complaint with the city police station on Oct 8.The suspects were identified as Rehan Anwar Sheikh (20), a resident of Shaniwar Peth, and Shubham Suresh Hadge (19), a resident of Kesarkar Peth. The minor has also been taken into custody.S G Mhetre, police inspector, Satara City police, said, “The incident happened on Oct 7th at midnight. The suspected gang broke open the shutters of Avadhoot Jewellers shop. They stole gold rings worth Rs1.30 lakh, nose rings worth Rs1.25 lakh, silver bangles and anklets worth Rs1.53 lakh each, silver ornaments worth Rs55,000, small and large idols worth Rs33,000 and rings, zodiac stones, and tax money from the shop.The next day after the incident, the city police conducted a panchnama and immediately started an investigation.The jeweller’s shop had a CCTV camera. However, it came to light that the thieves also stole the entire set of machines, including the DVR and CCTV camera, during the robbery, which hampered the police’s preliminary investigation.“While the investigation was going on through technical and conventional information, some suspects were seen in the CCTV footage that was gathered from the area. The suspects were then arrested, who confessed to the theft,” added Mhetre.
Article Summary: The Satara city police have arrested three suspects, including a minor, for allegedly breaking open the shutter of a jewellery shop. The theft took place on the night of Oct 7. The suspects were identified as Rehan Anwar Sheikh (20), a resident of Shaniwar Peth, and Shubham Suresh Hadge (19) The minor has also been taken into custody.

Article Title: Mumbai-bound traffic hit after hatchback catches fire on Vashi Creek bridge
Article Text:
The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine.





NAVI MUMBAI: Vehicular traffic from Navi Mumbai towards Mumbai was disrupted for around 30 minutes after a hatchback caught fire while crossing the Vashi Creek Bridge on Friday at around 7.30pm.The driver escaped unhurt. He immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. However, the fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred.Vashi traffic police alerted the Vashi fire brigade, which reached the spot within 15 minutes. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.Sunil Kadam, senior inspector of the Vashi traffic unit, said the driver was identified as Sumit Bhikaji Kadam.“At around 7.45pm, we received a call from one Rahul, whose full name is not known, informing us that a car had caught fire on the Mumbai-bound lane of the Vashi Creek Bridge,” said AV Sisode, the on-duty fireman at Vashi fire station.“In the meantime, we also received a call from the Vashi traffic police and immediately rushed to the spot with a fire tender. The Mumbai fire brigade team had also reached the spot as there was some confusion over the jurisdiction,” Sisode said.The fire was subsequently extinguished, and the Vashi fire brigade team returned to the station at around 8.30pm.
Article Summary: The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. The fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.

Article Title: Mumbai-Goa highway crash: 30-year-old killed, 2 cousins injured after Honda City hits gate
Article Text:
30-year-old Akshay Kadam lost his life in a car accident after he lost control of his vehicle





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man driving his Honda City car was killed and his two friends, both paternal cousin brothers accompanying him were injured after the driver lost control over the wheels on the Mangaon-Mahad stretch of Mumbai-Goa highway after crossing Mangaon railway station and veering off the road crashed into the iron gate of an industrial unit.The fatal accident occured on Monday around 3 am, when the three friends had gone for dinner at a roadside food stall in Mangaon and were returning to their respective villages in Mahad taluka.The injured complainant stated in the FIR registered at Mangaon police station that the accused car driver and his cousin had consumed liquor before going for dinner.The deceased driver was identified as Akshay Arjun Kadam, a resident of Nandgaon, Mahad taluka. Those injured are Rohit Rajendra Dhadve (24), working as safety officer at Astriel Life Science Pvt Ltd in Mahad MIDC and his cousin Roshan Dilip Dhadve (24). Both residents of Kembhurli, Mahad taluka.Maruti Andhale, senior inspector of Mangaon said, "As the complainant Rohit Dhadve has stated in the FIR that the accused Akshay Kadam drove the car after consuming liquor along with his cousin Roshan, when they had meet near the bus stop, after which they went to Mangaon for dinner, the Motor Vehicle Act section for drunk driving will be invoked.However, as the accused car driver Akshay Kadam responsible for the car crash had died in the accident, a final closure 'Abated summary' report will be submitted before the Mangaon magistrate court. "As per the FIR by the complainant Rohit Dhadve, on Sept 28 around 1 am, when he was at home, his paternal cousin Roshan spoke to him over mobile, when Roshan's maternal cousin Akshay Kadam accompanying him told Rohit that he had come from Mumbai and asked him to meet near the bus stand at Kembhurli.When Rohit met them at the spot, Roshan and Akshay were consuming liquor inside Akshay's Honda City car. Thereafter, Akshay said, "Let's go to Mangaon to have food and the three of them went in the car with Akshay at the wheels."Roshan was sitting beside Akshay and Rohit on the rear seat. They reached Mangaon around 2 am, where they ate parathas at a road side food stall and took parcel of Khima Pav.Thereafter, they drove for 3 kms towards Indapur and took a U-turn to return to their villages in Mahad.After crossing 300 metres from Mangaon railway Station, Akshay lost control over the wheels and yanking off the road on the right side, he crashed into the iron gate of Sundha Steel Traders industrial unit.Rohit sustained injuries below his left eye, left hand and left knee. Akshay got stuck between the driver's seat and the door. Roshan's left leg was injured.Hearing the loud noice of the car crash, the locals gathered, removed the three injured out of the car and summoned 108 ambulance in which they were rushed to Mangaon sub-district hospital, where Akshay was declared brought dead on arrival.
Article Summary: Akshay Arjun Kadam, 30, lost his life in a car accident after he lost control of his vehicle on the Mumbai-Goa highway. His two friends, both paternal cousin brothers accompanying him were injured. The three friends had gone for dinner at a roadside food stall in Mangaon.

Article Title: Unique tumour removal on pet a first in India: Veterinarian
Article Text:
Shih Tzu, Angel, along with her pet parent and Dr Narendra Pardeshi of Small Animal Clinic





PUNE: When blood persisted in the urine of 15-year-old city-based pet Shih Tzu ‘Angel’ for six months, veterinarians’ tests foud two 2cm-sized tumours in her urinary bladder, later diagnosed as an aggressive transitional cell carcinoma (TCC).Considering Angel’s advanced age, small size and nature of her cancer, doctors opted for minimally invasive Transurethral Resection of Urinary Bladder Tumour (TURBT) over conventional surgery. Its success on Sept 11 gave a new lease on life to Angel, to the relief of her loving family based in Lohegaon. Vets also believe it could be a first-of-its-kind TURBT on a pet animal in India.Dr Radheshyam Chaudhari, Urosurgeon at Small Animal Clinic in Pimple Saudagar, said, “She weighed just 5.6kg. Due to location of the tumours, we wanted to avoid putting her through major abdominal surgery if a safe alternative was possible.”Dr Narendra Pardeshi, veterinary surgeon at the clinic, said,”The approach is routinely used in human medicine and allowed us to apply minimally invasive technology and avoid the trauma associated with conventional open surgery.”
Article Summary: 15-year-old city-based pet Shih Tzu ‘Angel’ had two 2cm-sized tumours in her urinary bladder. Doctors opted for minimally invasive Transurethral Resection of Urinary Bladder Tumour (TURBT) over conventional surgery.

Article Title: Fire breaks out in a 22nd-floor flat at Balewadi
Article Text:
Representative image

Pune:





A fire broke out in the 22nd-floor flat at Balewadi on Saturday evening. There were no casualties but the furniture and electronic goods were destroyed.Station fire officer Shivaji Memane said the fire broke out around 4.30 pm. “We received an emergency call at 4.35 pm when residents of the building spotted flames coming out of the windows. We reached the spot with three fire tenders and a team entered the flat by breaking the door open. The furniture and electronic goods had become charcoal by the time we entered the flat.”“The family had gone out when the fire broke out. We are investigating the reason behind the fire,” he added.
Article Summary: A fire broke out in the 22nd-floor flat at Balewadi on Saturday evening. There were no casualties but the furniture and electronic goods were destroyed. Residents of the building spotted flames coming out of the windows. Station fire officer Shivaji Memane: We are investigating the reason behind the fire.

Article Title: Run for Unity Marathon on Nov 1, Mohol expects over 40k participants
Article Text:
Representative image

Pune:





The second leg of Run for Unity Marathon will be held in the city on Nov 1.MP Muralidhar Mohol on Saturday said over 40,000 people are expected to participate in the run in various categories, while declaring the details of the event. “Last year around 25,000 people had registered for the event; however, this year the registration has already reached 26,000 and is likely to cross the 40,000 mark. Some international runners and athletes are also participating in the event being held to mark the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.”The participation is open for the beginner run, 3km, 5km, 10km, 10-mile and half marathon. The runs in all categories will begin from Alka Talkies chowk in phases and will end at FC campus. This year the event will spread a message of “Nasha Mukta Yuva for Vikasit Bharat”.Cash prizes worth Rs10 lakh will be distributed to the winners from various categories. The organisers have approached Maha Metro to make adequate arrangements for the travel of participants on the event day.
Article Summary: The second leg of Run for Unity Marathon will be held in the city on Nov 1. Over 40,000 people are expected to participate in the run in various categories. The runs in all categories will begin from Alka Talkies chowk in phases and will end at FC campus.

Article Title: Before Navratri, mother returns home after two years
Article Text:
Nagpur:





Just before Navratri , a family in Chhattisgarh got its biggest reason to celebrate as a woman, missing for nearly two years, returned home after a 10-month search by Nagpur’s Regional Mental Hospital staff.The emotional reunion this week saw her son break down in tears, thanking the hospital team.The reunion, ahead of World Mental Health Day on October 10, highlighted how sustained care, compassion and coordination between healthcare workers and police can restore hope and bring families together.The son recalled that his father had died when he was just 14 and the family had feared that his mother was dead too.“You saved us from becoming orphans,” the son told the hospital staff.The 45-year-old woman was admitted to the Regional Mental Hospital on Jan 2, following an order from the chief judicial magistrate of Bhandara. She had been brought by police for treatment but had no identity documents and was unable to clearly state her name or address.The woman also gave different names for herself, while language difficulties made tracing her family even harder. Psychiatric treatment by doctors Pankaj Bagde and Krunali Uke gradually improved her mental health.As the woman recovered, her longing to return home and meet her children grew stronger. Social service superintendent Kunda Katkhaye Bidkar spent months counselling the woman and following every clue she provided.The hospital contacted around nine police stations across Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh but the search initially yielded no results. A breakthrough came when the woman mentioned her daughter’s marriage and relatives in Korba district.Bidkar sought help from a coordinator at Mother Teresa Ashram in Raipur and contacted Korba police. Inspector Narhari Patel of Korba police pursued the lead and contacted his counterpart at Ratanpur police station in Jabalpur.Within just three hours, the woman’s son was traced, bringing months of painstaking efforts to a successful end.The mother and son first saw each other over a video call. Both became emotional, and within two days, her son and son-in-law reached the hospital to take her home.Hospital staff gave the woman clothes and accessories as farewell gifts.Medical superintendent Dr Amrish Mohbe said mental healthcare went beyond medicines and included reconnecting patients with their families and society.
Article Summary: The 45-year-old woman was admitted to the Regional Mental Hospital on Jan 2, following an order from the chief judicial magistrate of Bhandara. She had been brought by police for treatment but had no identity documents and was unable to clearly state her name or address. Psychiatric treatment by doctors Pankaj Bagde and Krunali Uke gradually improved her mental health.

Article Title: MP farm caretaker couple killed in hit-and-run
Article Text:
Amravati:





A farm caretaker couple from Madhya Pradesh was killed in a hit-and-run accident near Maywadi Phata on the Morshi road on Friday night.The deceased have been identified as Somlal Uike (55) and his wife Chaturbati Uike (48), residents of Gazadhaba village in Multai tehsil of Betul district, Madhya Pradesh. The couple was currently working as caretakers at an agricultural field in Dapori village under Morshi taluka.As per the police, the incident took place around 8:30pm on Friday. The couple had come to Morshi for some work on their motorcycle and was returning to Dapori when an unidentified speeding vehicle rammed into their bike from behind near Maywadi Phata.Chaturbati Uike died on the spot after being run over. Her husband Somlal sustained critical injuries and died on the way to the Sub-District Hospital in Morshi.A team from Morshi police station rushed to the spot under the guidance of police inspector Rahul Athawale. PSI Deepak Uike and constable Balu Chavan conducted the spot panchnama. The bodies were shifted to the mortuary at the Sub-District Hospital, Morshi.A post-mortem was conducted on Saturday by medical officials and the bodies were handed over to the relatives of the deceased.Morshi police have registered a case against the unidentified driver for rash and negligent driving and causing death by negligence. Police are scanning CCTV footage from establishments along the Morshi route to trace the offending vehicle, PI Athawale said.
Article Summary: A farm caretaker couple from Madhya Pradesh was killed in a hit-and-run accident. The deceased have been identified as Somlal Uike and his wife Chaturbati Uike. The couple was working as caretakers at an agricultural field in Morshi taluka.
